title: 2.1.11 Nest a Check
description: Write an if statement inside another if statement to ask a follow-up question. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: composition of book 2.1.1 'The if Statement' and 2.1.3 'The else Clause'; curriculum-plan §2.1 Topics: Nested conditionals

steps.title: Declare two variables
steps.instructions: Create a variable called isLoggedIn (true or false) and a variable called isAdmin (true or false).

steps.title: Nest the admin check inside the login check
steps.instructions: Write an outer if that checks isLoggedIn. Inside that block, write a nested if / else that checks isAdmin: log 'Welcome, admin.' if true, log 'Welcome, user.' if false. Add an outer else that logs 'Please log in.'

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[set isLoggedIn and isAdmin]
  B --> C{logged in}
  C -- no --> D[/log Please log in/]
  C -- yes --> E{admin}
  E -- yes --> F[/log Welcome, admin/]
  E -- no --> G[/log Welcome, user/]
  D --> H([End])
  F --> H
  G --> H

requirements.title: isAdmin check nested inside isLoggedIn, logs admin message
requirements.description: if (isLoggedIn) nests an if (isAdmin) whose block logs a message about admin. Help: 2.1.9 (Nested Conditionals)

requirements.title: isAdmin's else logs user message
requirements.description: the else paired with if (isAdmin) logs a message about user. Help: 2.1.9 (Nested Conditionals)

requirements.title: outer else logs please log in
requirements.description: the outer else (paired with isLoggedIn) logs a message containing 'log in'. Help: 2.1.9 (Nested Conditionals)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.1.11 Nest a Check". The task they were given: Create a variable called isLoggedIn (true or false) and a variable called isAdmin (true or false). You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
